name: Cincinnati Art Museum

facts.text: Free loan wheelchairs are available without reservations in the coatrooms near the Main and Dewitt entrances. Accessible parking and front-entrance drop-off are described on the museum's access page.
The Welcome Cart lends headphones, earplugs and fidgets. A private quiet space is on the ground floor across from the coatroom.
Social narratives, visual timers and a large-print access guide help visitors prepare and identify quieter spaces.
Benches are distributed through the museum. Visitors who must shorten a ticketed exhibition visit can request an accessibility re-entry ticket.

limitations: Public website information; no on-site audit. Re-entry accommodation must be requested. Confirm specific restroom, route and equipment needs with the museum.

name: Cincinnati Museum Center

facts.text: The far-left and far-right historic entrance doors have automatic push-plate controls. Wheelchairs and ECVs can be rented at the box office, first come, first served.
Universal restrooms on Mezzanine B and the lower level near Westheimer Gallery have adult changing tables.
The visitor page links to accessibility and sensory maps.
Visitors may bring food and drinks for seated dining areas; these are prohibited in museums, exhibitions and the OMNIMAX theater.

limitations: Public website information; no on-site audit. Rentals require an adult renter, agreement and retained ID or credit card; availability is not guaranteed. Request entry assistance at least 24 hours ahead.

name: Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden

facts.text: Calming rooms are listed at Vine Street Village and Mai Thai's Market. Sensory bags are available to check out at the Welcome Center.
The Zoo publishes social and video narratives for general visits and several individual experiences.
Selected family restrooms include adult changing tables. A courtesy cart can assist visitors with mobility concerns along a fixed return route to Vine Street Village.
An Access Pass lets visitors who have significant difficulty standing or waiting queue outside the physical line for selected rides and experiences, with the same wait time.

limitations: Public website information; no on-site audit. Courtesy cart service is first come, first served. Ride restrictions and mobility-device transfer requirements vary; check the official guide. Address source: https://cincinnatizoo.org/plan-your-adventure/

name: Taft Museum of Art

facts.text: The museum lists ramps, elevators, lifts, accessible restrooms and wheelchairs. Ask the admissions team for a wheelchair or lift assistance.
A quiet room and noise-reducing headphones are available. Admissions provides Braille and large-print visitor materials.
The museum's carry-in policy permits water for medical purposes; otherwise outside food and drink are prohibited.

limitations: Public website information; no on-site audit. Confirm individual accommodation needs with accessibility@taftmuseum.org.

name: Contemporary Arts Center

facts.text: The 6th Street entrance is at street level with an automatic door. Elevators reach all floors. Accessible restrooms are on all floors except the lobby.
The front desk lends wheelchairs, stools, hearing amplifiers, large-print exhibition text and sensory bags without charge.
Sensory bags include a narrative and map. Free tours for visitors with memory loss and their caregivers can be arranged with two weeks' notice.
ASL interpretation for public programs and audio-described tours require two weeks' notice.

limitations: Public website information; no on-site audit. Confirm scheduled accommodations with the center. Gallery access may change during exhibition installation.

name: Cincinnati Playhouse in the Park

facts.text: Wheelchair seating is available in both theaters; the Rouse Theatre also offers transfer seats. Request these when reserving tickets.
Both theaters use hearing loops compatible with T-coil devices and offer hearing-enhancement receivers. Large-print programs are available from ushers.
Selected sensory-friendly/relaxed performances accommodate visitors who benefit from a more relaxed setting; check the performance calendar.
ASL and audio description are offered on designated performance dates.

limitations: Public website information; no on-site audit. Accessible garage parking is limited and requires advance reservation and payment, plus a valid placard. Accessible seats are subject to availability.

name: Aronoff Center for the Arts

facts.text: Accessible seating is offered in all theaters. For Procter & Gamble Hall, enter at street level and use elevators to reach the appropriate seating level.
A courtesy wheelchair can assist visitors between the lobby and seats, first come, first served.
Assistive listening devices are available at Guest Services in the Procter & Gamble Hall Marble Lobby. Audio description and ASL performances can be requested at least three weeks ahead.

limitations: Public website information; no on-site audit. Contact the ticket office in advance for seating and performance-specific accommodations.

name: Cincinnati Music Hall

facts.text: The accessible entrance is on Elm Street at the southeast side. South elevators serve every level, including the Ballroom; a north elevator also serves all levels.
Access Ambassadors at the southeast entrance provide wayfinding and seat assistance; wheelchairs can be requested for transport from curb or lobby to seats.
Guest Services in the Lindner Grand Foyer provides assistive listening devices with a neck loop for T-coil users.
First-aid services are located in the North Concourse on the Orchestra level; ask staff for assistance.

limitations: Public website information; no on-site audit. Arrange special seating with the box office in advance when possible.

name: Downtown Main Library

facts.text: Accessible parking is in the gated lot north of 9th Street. Use the intercom with a disability parking placard visible; staff assistance entering the library can be requested.
The South Plaza is at street level. The location page directs visitors to the Vine Street or Walnut Street entrances because the 9th Street entrance is closed.
A downloadable building map is available, with free printed copies at the library.

limitations: Public website information; no on-site audit. Entrance closure is time-sensitive. Confirm the route and facilities needed for your visit.

name: Harrison Branch Library

facts.text: The branch's official facility list identifies accessible facilities.
The branch lists both curbside service and a drive-through.

limitations: Public website information; no on-site audit. The facility list does not specify door widths, restroom layout or sensory conditions. Contact the branch for details.

name: Winton Woods

facts.text: Great Parks lists an accessible canoe/kayak transfer launch at the harbor and an accessible playground at Harper Meadows.
A Zero G-Chair swing is listed at Winton Woods.

limitations: Public website information; no on-site audit. Verify current launch operation and park closures. Address source: https://www.greatparks.org/parks/winton-woods

name: Miami Whitewater Forest

facts.text: An accessible canoe/kayak launch uses a sliding transfer bench.
The park has a Zero G-Chair swing; the golf course offers reservable Solo Rider carts.

limitations: Public website information; no on-site audit. Confirm availability before visiting. Address source: https://www.greatparks.org/parks/miami-whitewater-forest

name: Sharon Woods

facts.text: Great Parks lists an accessible playground and a Zero G-Chair swing.
Sharon Woods is specifically excluded from Great Parks' blanket statement about accessible paved shared-use trails.

limitations: Public website information; no on-site audit. Harbor construction affects amenities; check closures. Address and construction source: https://www.greatparks.org/parks/sharon-woods

name: Francis RecreAcres

facts.text: The accessible playground includes rubber surfacing and wide ramps.
The park page lists an easy, one-mile shared-use loop passing the playground and soccer fields.

limitations: Public website information; no on-site audit. Confirm current conditions. Address source: https://www.greatparks.org/parks/francis-recreacres

name: Pyramid Hill Sculpture Park & Museum

facts.text: Paved routes run through the park, but some have steep hills or uneven ground. A ramp for the Visitor Center is available on request.
Wheelchair-accessible restrooms are listed in the Pyramid House and Gallery Museum during museum hours. The Pavilion restroom building has a small entrance step.
The mobile web app offers recorded sculpture descriptions. Docents in the Pyramid House can provide 3D copies of selected sculptures for tactile study.
Call the park about reserving an Art Cart for mobility needs; rentals depend on weather and availability.

limitations: Public website information; no on-site audit. The page describes a wheelchair-accessible Gallery Museum entrance but also a small step; confirm the step-free route directly before relying on it.

name: Cincinnati Nature Center — Rowe Woods

facts.text: The center describes the 0.72-mile Mashburn Family Discovery Trail as all-accessible.
Designated accessible parking is listed at the Rowe Visitor Center, Krippendorf Lodge and Nature PlayScape lots.
Other trails vary in surface and slope, with some rocky creek crossings, steep stairs or inclines. Visitor Services can discuss routes and accommodation needs.

limitations: Public website information; no on-site audit. An accessible designation for the Discovery Trail does not apply to all Rowe Woods trails. Confirm surface conditions and route suitability.

name: Bettman Nature Preserve & Center

facts.text: Cincinnati Parks describes a paved wheelchair-accessible path leading to views of the preserve.

limitations: Public website information from the official park search result; full-page retrieval was unreliable. No on-site audit. Building, restroom and other trail accessibility were not established.

name: National Underground Railroad Freedom Center

facts.text: Elevators connect each floor. Accessible restrooms are listed on the first, third and fourth floors. Wheelchairs and ECVs are available from the front desk, first come, first served.
A Braille museum map is available at check-in. Permanent-gallery videos have open captions, while temporary-exhibition audio is transcribed in panels or guides.
A Visual Welcome Guide is available to prepare for a museum visit.
The museum reports accessibility carts on the second and third floors with headphones, fidgets and sunglasses.

limitations: Public website information; no on-site audit. Rentals cannot leave the museum; ECV rental has a fee and agreement requirements. Confirm equipment and accommodation availability.
